fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Papal Bulls as the Legal Foundation", "body": "Dylan Saccoccio walked through four papal bulls from his book, Unam Sanctam, Romanus Pontifex, Aeterni Regis and the 1542 bull of the Council of Trent, and argued that together they formed the paper basis for claims over land, subjects and souls. He described them as the three crowns of Baal and said their wording about perpetual remembrance showed how the system was meant to last forever. When Dylan could not recall the meaning of indult, one of the hosts supplied a definition. Dylan said his goal was awareness, not courtroom battle. These were Dylan's readings, offered as his own research."}, {"title": "Etymology and Star Lore in Legalese", "body": "Wordplay ran through the whole show. Dylan argued that canon, bail, magistrate and common all carried older religious or maritime meanings, and he tied the Holy See to the sea. Gabe read Black's Law Dictionary entries for enemy and noted that approaching the bar echoed navigation by the stars. One of the hosts also relayed work developed with John McHugh placing the origin of contracts in the Pegasus Square, and Chance previewed a coming interview on the astrology behind biblical stories. One of the hosts called a birth and tribe anagram possibly anecdotal and said to file it away."}, {"title": "Trusts, Birth Certificates and Personhood", "body": "Dylan laid out his claim that a birth certificate created a legal fiction, the all caps name, held in three Cestui Que Vie trusts covering real property, personal property and the soul through baptism. He explained capitis diminutio as three degrees of lost status shown in how a name was capitalized, and cited cases defining a person in commerce. One of the hosts stressed that, in Dylan's account, the living human was never the legal slave. Dylan also drew on his past work in real estate and financial services to illustrate how trusts shield wealth."}, {"title": "The 1933 Banking Act Argument", "body": "Dylan argued that the 1933 Emergency Banking Relief Act and its amendment of the Trading with the Enemy Act turned public debt into a trust with citizens as collateral. He read a 1993 speech by James Traficant on bankruptcy, which called the Federal Reserve a maritime lender, and a Congressional Record quote attributed to Patman. Gabe read Black's Law Dictionary definitions of enemy aloud. One of the hosts suggested the enemy might mean state citizens, and Dylan said it was possible but he did not know. Dylan framed the Social Security Act and earlier birth registration laws as further steps in the same pattern."}, {"title": "Opting Out and Staying Aware", "body": "Dylan repeated that he did not recommend fighting the system in court, only learning how it worked so people could avoid entering it, and he pointed to others better suited for legal battles. One of the hosts argued that fear of consequences was the real coercion and that people who left the rat race found a way to survive. A later exchange covered fixed rate debt, with one speaker saying inflation could work in a borrower's favor while stressing it was not advice. Gabe closed with Clint Richardson's idea that a solution is the end of a contract, and Chance plugged his merch store."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dylan Saccoccio returns to provide some guidance on the origins and scope of legal sorcery and its connection to priestcraft, based off the information in his second Spirit Whirled book, The Blackest of All Magick. Black's Law dictionary is darker than you thought!
